generation.explanation: A radian is a way of measuring angles using the circle itself: it is the central angle formed when the arc length along the circle is exactly equal to the radius. Since angle = arc length / radius (θ = s/r), one radian is about 57.3°, and a full circle (s = 2πr) is 2π ≈ 6.28 radians. In the animation, watch the radius sweep out until the yellow arc has the same length as r — that angle is exactly 1 radian. Then drag the orange point around the circle or use the slider to see how arc length, radians, and degrees stay linked.
